reference_memory.normal_pattern: The normal pattern exhibits a robust quasi-periodic oscillation with a dominant period of ~77 points, consistent across all candidates. Each cycle contains a sharp, symmetric negative excursion (trough) reaching -18 to -20 standardized units, followed by a slower, smoother recovery to baseline near 0. The troughs are narrow (~15–20 points wide) and steep on the descent (slope ~-1.0 to -1.3 per point), with a slightly gentler ascent (~+0.6 to +0.8 per point). Baseline is stable near median 0 (±0.04), with low-amplitude high-frequency noise (MAD ~0.6–0.75) superimposed. Roughness (~0.16–0.20) and curvature (~0.16–0.24) metrics confirm smooth, low-variability morphology outside troughs. Amplitude at 90th percentile is consistently ~18–20, indicating predictable extremal behavior. No sustained trend is present across cycles; slope per point averages near zero (±0.05), though minor local drifts occur. Boundary truncation is evident in candidate 0 (single-cycle slice ending abruptly in a trough), but the core motif—sharp dip + slow rebound—is preserved across all candidates. Acceptable variation includes slight differences in trough depth (±1 unit), exact timing of onset (±2–3 points), and minor baseline wobble (<0.2 units). Noise remains homoscedastic and uncorrelated with cycle phase.

Three-cycle (3P) segment with three well-resolved, nearly identical troughs centered near indices 950, 1025, and 1095. Each trough reaches ~-20, symmetric descent/ascent, clean baseline near 0. Minor baseline drift (<0.1) between cycles. High fidelity representation of canonical motif.

Three-cycle (3P) segment mirroring candidate 1 in structure: three deep troughs (~-20) with consistent shape and spacing. Slight baseline offset (-0.04 median) and marginally steeper ascent slopes. No anomalies; morphology fully aligns with consensus.

Five-cycle (5P) segment confirming long-term stability: five troughs spaced evenly (~77 pts), each reaching ~-20. Slightly higher MAD (0.75) and roughness (0.198) suggest marginally more noise or micro-variation, but no structural deviation. Final cycle truncated at rebound peak—still captures full trough morphology.

reference_memory.selection_guidance: Prefer candidates 1 or 2 for query matching when ≥3 cycles are available; they provide highest-fidelity templates for trough shape, timing, and baseline. Use candidate 3 for longer queries (>300 pts) to assess multi-cycle consistency. Candidate 0 is only suitable for single-cycle queries where only partial morphology is observable; treat its truncated trough as incomplete, not anomalous. When a query shows a trough deeper than -21 or asymmetric (e.g., slow descent/fast ascent), it diverges from all references and should be flagged.
uncertainties: Exact trough width tolerance (15–22 pts) not quantified per cycle
Whether minor baseline offsets (±0.05) reflect true stationarity or residual trend
High-frequency noise structure (e.g., autocorrelation) not inferable from plots alone
Potential for very rare 'flat' cycles without troughs—none observed in references
